pages.text: Asphalt makes dark, clean roads and floors. It is made from the heaviest part of crude oil.

$(l)Bitumen$()$(br)In a mechanical press over a $(item)heated$() basin, $(item)1000 mB of heavy oil$() compacts into one $(item)bitumen$(). A burning firebox or a lit blaze burner under the basin is enough.

$(l)Asphalt mixture$()$(br)In a mixer: $(item)sand + bitumen + gravel$() gives $(item)16 asphalt mixture$(). With $(item)slag$() instead of sand, you get $(item)32$().$(br2)$(l)Liquid asphalt$()$(br)$(item)Asphalt mixture + 250 mB water$() gives $(item)1000 mB liquid asphalt$(), in a Create mixer or in a chemical vat with an industrial mixer.

$(l)Laying it$()$(br)Pour liquid asphalt like liquid concrete: it $(item)hardens into asphalt blocks$() after a short random delay. Spread it with a bucket for small paths, or with a Create hose pulley for long roads.
In a stonecutter, one asphalt block gives $(item)2 slabs$(), or stairs, or a wall, for kerbs and ramps.$(br2)One bitumen becomes 16 to 32 blocks of road, so a single heavy oil tank goes a long way.
